title: Grace and works
hookLine: Catholics and Lutherans agreed in 1999 that we're saved by grace, not by works, and good works follow

cards: In the city where Lutherans had once presented their confession of faith to the emperor, leaders of the Lutheran World Federation and of the Catholic Church sit down at one table and sign a document together.
For centuries, the two churches had formally condemned each other's teaching on how a person is made right with God. Wars had been fought partly over it. Families split.
Now they sign a statement saying: on the heart of this question, we agree. Not on everything. On the center.

teach.b: Justification is a courtroom word. To justify someone is to declare them in the right. In the Bible, the question is: how does a person come to be right with God?
Paul's answer, in Ephesians, is the line from day two hundred eighty-nine: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God."
And the very next lines go on: "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works." Grace first. Then good.
But James says bluntly: "faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone." For centuries, Protestants and Catholics heard those texts pulling in different directions.

Lutherans stressed that God declares sinners righteous, a free gift received by faith alone. Catholics stressed that God's grace truly makes a person righteous from within, and works through a changed life.
Each suspected the other of missing something.

The Joint Declaration put the shared center like this, in summary: by grace alone, through faith in what Christ has done, and not by anything people have earned, God accepts them and gives the Holy Spirit, who renews hearts and calls people to good works.
Both sides agreed the old condemnations don't apply to the teaching as the other now presents it. They still describe some things differently, and some theologians on both sides objected.
Since then, world bodies of Methodist, Anglican and Reformed churches have affirmed it too.

teach.h: CREATED IN CHRIST JESUS UNTO GOOD WORKS.
teach.b: The order fits in a pocket: grace comes first, and good works grow out of it, the way fruit grows on a tree that is already alive.

how: Christians across the churches describe good works, such as serving the poor, giving and caring for neighbors, as a grateful response to God's grace, and some churches mark Reformation Day on October 31 with joint Catholic–Lutheran prayer.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: Catholics teach that people earn salvation by good works
the Joint Declaration says Catholics and Lutherans agree we're accepted by grace, not because of anything we deserve.
the declaration says the old condemnations don't apply to each other's teaching as now presented
both sides said so, while some differences in how they describe things remain.

games.q: Augsburg, 1999. after centuries of mutual condemnation, Catholics and Lutherans sit down at one table. what do they sign?
o: a full merger of the two churches.
a declaration that on the heart of justification they agree.
a statement that the argument never mattered.
games.why: the Joint Declaration said both agree on the center: by grace alone, through faith, with good works following. the old condemnations don't apply to each other's teaching as now presented.

practice: Remember something you've been given that you didn't earn, and stay with it for a few breaths.
Then, out of that thankfulness, not out of guilt or to prove anything, choose one small, specific good thing to do today: a call, a meal, a note, a chore done for someone else.
If you pray, thank God for grace and offer the good work as thanks; if you don't, just let gratitude choose it.

wordCard.voice: Justification. Being made right with God. Catholics and Lutherans now agree: by grace, through faith, and good works follow.

orig.note: Greek: to justify, to declare or make righteous. Paul's word in Romans and Galatians.

carryVoice: Your line: grace first, then good. Thanks, not fear, does the choosing. Day three hundred nine, done.
